html:
On 1 April 1999 Canada created the territory of Nunavut, meaning "our land" in Inuktitut, out of the eastern part of the Northwest Territories. It covers about a fifth of Canada, with a population of under 40,000, most of them Inuit.

It came from the Nunavut Land Claims Agreement of 1993, the largest Indigenous land claim settlement in Canadian history, which gave Inuit title to a large area and a share of resource revenues.

Its capital is Iqaluit on Baffin Island, and Inuktitut is an official language. Nunavut faces high costs, housing shortages and youth suicide. It follows Inuit self rule in Greenland and is home to the descendants of the Thule people and earlier the Dorset.
